repairRoute: A: a client outside the Codex PreToolUse hook (Claude Code), per rules/codex-edit-guard-repair.md P4
detection: The owner instructed a Codex session in this repository to change the viewport rules. Codex stopped without editing and reported that required reading was refused by the guard. The owner reported it as a problem: owner-directed Codex work was blocked by a Claude-built control.

evidence.output: EDIT GUARD: Edit path is outside repository.
evidence.selftestBeforeFix: passed: true. The approved route {op:"required", path:"vault/WORKFLOW.md"} delivered every document; it was never used.

cause: The guard served upper-layer documents only through op "required" with a list key. An agent asking with op "read" and the document's absolute path was refused, although the document is on the approved list.
The refusal reused the edit-path validator, so a read was reported as "Edit path is outside repository." and named no working route. The agent could not recover from the message.
fix: op "read" with the exact absolute path of an approved document returns the same document through readRequiredDocument (same link/hard-link/realpath checks). The readable set is unchanged.
Any other read outside the repository is still refused, now as "Read path is outside repository" with the read-command required usage.
selftest checks absolute-path delivery for every approved document; the e2e adds a group for delivery, the mapping and the refusal text.

p5.selftest: exit 0; 53 ok, 0 failed; absolute path arrives for 21/21 approved documents
mutation: absolute-path mapping disabled on a copy: e2e exit 1 (killed)
refusal message reverted to the edit-path validator on a copy: e2e exit 1 (killed)

notChanged: Edit admission. The Codex session is bound only to one report file, so editing rules/ would still be refused as out of scope, and builds, tests and git remain operator-terminal work. Whether this guard should stay armed for maintenance of this repository is an owner decision and was reported, not changed.
.codex/hooks.json and the /hooks trust state were not touched; the hook definition is unchanged, so no re-trust is needed.
